entities.summary:
NVIDIA Corporation is an American multinational technology company founded in 1993 by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky, and Curtis Priem in Santa Clara, California. Originally a graphics processing unit (GPU) manufacturer for gaming, it became the world's most valuable semiconductor company and the essential infrastructure provider for artificial intelligence.

NVIDIA's invention of the GPU in 1999 transformed computer graphics, enabling real-time 3D rendering that powered the gaming and visual effects industries. The development of CUDA parallel computing platform in 2006 unexpectedly made NVIDIA GPUs essential for scientific computing, deep learning research, and cryptocurrency mining. The 2012 ImageNet deep learning breakthrough by Alex Krizhevsky's team using NVIDIA GPUs demonstrated that AI training required massive parallel computation.

The AI boom following ChatGPT's launch in 2022 created unprecedented demand for NVIDIA's H100 GPUs, used to train large language models. NVIDIA's market capitalization surpassed $3 trillion in 2024, making it the most valuable company in the world. Every major AI lab — OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Anthropic, Meta AI — depends on NVIDIA hardware, making the company the 'picks and shovels' provider of the AI gold rush.
